steps.title: Match each order to its customer
steps.change: Both sample orders match Anu, so both remain before the date filter.
steps.added_sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.City, o.OrderDate, o.Total_Order_Amount
FROM Customers AS c
INNER JOIN Orders AS o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
ORDER BY o.OrderID;
steps.sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.City, o.OrderDate, o.Total_Order_Amount
FROM Customers AS c
INNER JOIN Orders AS o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
ORDER BY o.OrderID;

steps.title: Filter to December 2025
steps.change: The reporting period applies to the entire result. January 2026 is outside the call sheet period.
steps.added_sql: WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2025' AND strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) = '12'
steps.sql:
SELECT o.OrderID, c.CustomerID, c.FirstName, c.LastName, c.City, o.OrderDate, o.Total_Order_Amount
FROM Customers AS c
INNER JOIN Orders AS o ON c.CustomerID = o.CustomerID
WHERE strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2025' AND strftime('%m', o.OrderDate) = '12'
ORDER BY o.OrderID;

steps.title: Format and sort the call sheet
steps.change: The support team needs readable customer names and cities. The ID breaks ties when orders have the same date.
steps.added_sql:
select o.OrderID, o.OrderDate, (c.FirstName||" "|| c.LastName) as customer_name, trim(c.City) as City, o.Total_Order_Amount
-- …
